newsitem.title: USA: Calif. plan would reshape Golden Eagle Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Calif. plan would reshape Golden Eagle Insurance.

text.p: California's Insurance Department unveiled plans on Tuesday to reshape Golden Eagle Insurance Co under new management less than a week after the company was seized by the state agency.

Golden Eagle, one of the largest writers of workers compensation insurance in California, was seized by the Department of Insurance last Friday because certain of its business practices put the company and consumers at risk, state Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said.

Under the Department of Insurance plan, which is subject to court approval, Golden Eagle Insurance will be renamed San Diego Casualty Insurance Co. The company and its employees will remain in San Diego, California, Quackenbush said.

An agreement in principle was reached between the state Insurance Department and the U.S. arm of the Zurich Centre Group, Insurance Partners L.P. and Superior National Insurance Co. The agreement should help to support Golden Eagle operations in their new form, Quackenbush said.
Under the agreement, Zurich Centre Group will continue to provide lines of insurance currently written by Golden Eagle.
These lines will include workers compensation coverage, personal passenger automobile and homeowners insurance and commercial automobile insurance, Quackenbush said.
"The agreement announced today contemplates the rehabilitation of Golden Eagle under new management and with strong financial backing," Quackenbush said.

Last Friday, Quackenbush served a court order to take over control and operation of Golden Eagle, citing a $138.5 million shortfall in cash reserves required by the state, and unsecured and questionable loans.

Golden Eagle owner John Mabee's ownership rights and equity in the company would remain with the shell of the old Golden Eagle along with all past non-insurance liabilities and lawsuits against Golden Eagle, Quackenbush said.
